questions.question: The responsibility of regulating and supervising primary (urban) cooperative banks, which are popularly known as Urban Cooperative Banks (UCBs) is vested with which one of the following?

options.text: The Department of Non-Banking Supervision of the Reserve Bank of India
The Urban Banks Department of the Reserve Bank of India
The Department of Corporate Services of the Reserve Bank of India

questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 2 i.e. __**The Urban Banks Department of the Reserve Bank of India.**__

 
• **Cooperative banks of India** are **registered as cooperative societies** where members from a community **band together to extend loans** to each other **at favourable terms.**
 
• Cooperative banks are broadly **classified** into **Urban or Rural Co-operative Banks** based on their region of operation.
 
• **Urban Cooperative banks** are further classified into **Scheduled and Non-Scheduled **banks.
 
• **UCBs** are only **partly regulated by the RBI.**
 
• While their **banking operations are regulated by the RBI,** which lays down their capital adequacy, risk control and lending norms,** their management and resolution in the case of distress are regulated by the Registrar of Co-operative Societies either under the State or Central government.**
 
• UCBs are structured as co-operatives, with their members carrying unlimited liability.
 
• In the event** UCBs fail,** deposits with them are covered by the **Deposit Insurance and Credit Guarantee Corporation of India **up to a **sum of ₹5 lakh per depositor.**

**Reserve Bank of India: **

 
• **HQ: Mumbai**
 
• **Governor - Sanjay Malhotra**

questions.question: According to the Constitution of India, how many members from the Anglo-Indian community can be nominated to the Lok Sabha by the President?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__2__**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **__Important Points__**The Anglo-Indian reserved seats in the Lok Sabha and state legislative assemblies of India were **discontinued **in January 2020 by the **104th **Constitutional Amendment Act of 2019.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Article 81 of the Constitution of India 1949 has specified the maximum strength of Members of Parliament in the Lok Sabha to be 550__.
 
• Earlier it was 552, but the provision of 2 nominated Anglo - Indian persons has now been removed.
 
• Out of the maximum permitted strength, not more than 530 members are to be chosen by direct election from territorial constituencies in the Indian states,
 
• Not more than 20 members are to represent the union territories, chosen in such manner as Parliament of India may by law provide.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**
